title: OpenRTB Native 1.2 bid pair signaled as push via imp.ext.adtype, icon and main image both required

source.name: IAB OpenRTB Native Ads 1.2 asset objects, carried in an OpenRTB 2.6 Bid.adm
source.notes: All source records are retained in assets/sources.json by reference.sourceIds.

modifications: All ids, domains, prices and creative text independently authored; icon (asset id 1, IAB Native 1.2 img.type=1 ICON) and main image (asset id 3, img.type=3 MAIN) are both required assets, differentiating this pair from push-exads-openrtb-native-500 (icon-only, no main image, vendor plcmttype=500).

imp.ext.adtype="push" is this project's own non-IAB extension-detection convention (packages/core/non-iab-formats.js STRING_HINT_KEYS), not an IAB-standardized field and not attributed to a named vendor's documented contract — unlike push-exads-openrtb-native-500's vendor-specific native.request.plcmttype=500, this pair stays entirely inside plain Native 1.2 (plcmttype=1) and layers the push signal only in imp.ext.
bid.mtype=4 (NATIVE) is set explicitly, matching the asset payload, so response-side format detection does not depend on adm content-sniffing alone.
provenance.sanitized: No real user, device or tracking data. device.ip is the documentation-only address 192.0.2.44 (TEST-NET-1); user.id is a synthetic-fixture string; all domains use reserved .test hostnames; icon/image URLs are placeholders the preview's content policy never fetches automatically.

pairApplicability.note: A plain, spec-legal OpenRTB 2.6 Native 1.2 bid pair; the only non-IAB element is the imp.ext.adtype push hint, which is a project convention layered on top rather than a deviation from the Native/OpenRTB contract itself.

device.ua: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

bid.adm: {"native":{"ver":"1.2","link":{"url":"https://advertiser.example.test/offers/push-x-ext-rtb-native-push"},"assets":[{"id":1,"img":{"url":"https://assets.example.test/feeds/push-x-ext-rtb-native-push-icon-48x48.png","w":48,"h":48}},{"id":2,"title":{"text":"A rooftop herb garden"}},{"id":3,"img":{"url":"https://assets.example.test/feeds/push-x-ext-rtb-native-push-hero-300x150.png","w":300,"h":150}},{"id":4,"data":{"value":"Grow herbs in a small rooftop planter."}}],"imptrackers":["https://tracking.example.test/notice/push-x-ext-rtb-native-push-imp"]}}

specNotes: imp.ext.adtype is one of the STRING_HINT_KEYS non-iab-formats.js scans for on every imp; "push" normalizes into PUSH_FORMAT_NAMES, so imp.non_standard_format (INFO, oRTB 2.6 §3.2.4 Imp) is expected, alongside format-detect.js unioning PUSH into the request-side tags — this is the documented, generic non-IAB-format-hint mechanism, not a claim that "adtype" is an IAB-standardized key.

All 3 required Native 1.2 assets (icon id 1, title id 2, main image id 3) are present in bid.adm; crosscheck.bid.native_complete must report the full required set, matching the same contract push-exads-openrtb-native-500 already exercises with a icon-only required set.

bid.mtype=4 is an OpenRTB 2.6 addition (oRTB 2.6 §4.3 Bid); its presence is what version-detection promotes the response side from an assumed 2.5 baseline to a detected 2.6, which is why this pair — unlike the request-side-only-optional-fields case — is tagged protocol ortb-2.6 rather than ortb-2.5.

Desired capability: the format union carries both native and push for this pair (request-side ext hint plus response-side native asset detection); existing product acceptance is not the validity oracle.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.
